Okay. So go ahead. Joanne, are you presenting? Yeah, go ahead. Good evening, Chair Chapman
and members of Council. I am here this evening to present our recommendations for general
amendments to the signed bylaw. This work was prepared in response to Council's direction
in September 2023 to address excessive boulevard signage.
In addition, we have used this opportunity to address other general amendments
that have been identified through frequent use of the sign bylaw.
These changes are minor and technical and do not impact the overall intent of the sign bylaw.
On September 25, 2023, Council put forward a motion to address excessive boulevard signs,
which cause visual clutter and pose a safety hazard in the community.
Council's motion relates to special event directional signs.
These are small, freestanding signs used to direct traffic to the location of a special event.
They are allowed to be posted between the hours of 9 a.m. and 6 p.m. on the day of the event.
These signs are permitted in the boulevard, the area on city streets
between the traveled portion of the road and the sidewalk or the property line.
They are not permitted in the median.
New home builder signs are also permitted in the boulevard,
and those signs have their own regulations.
Staff are not proposing any changes to the new home builder sign regulations.
Staff reviewed the regulations of the sign bylaw
and are proposing the following changes
to allow the sign to be displayed for the entire day,
which gives flexibility for events that may start earlier than 9 a.m. or run later than 6 p.m.
Additionally, require the prominent display of either the date or the name of the day of the week
for special event directional signs to benefit residents and deter misuse,
and remove the provision in the sign bylaw that requires the 30-day sign hold after a sign has been removed
as the hold has been ineffective in addressing the issue of excessive boulevard signs
and holding these signs creates an administrative burden on bylaw enforcement staff.
Other proposed general amendments include updating the signed bylaw with zoning references
to align with the zoning bylaw, such as adding a list of permitted sign types in mixed-use zones
and including employment zones in the list of permitted sign types by zone.
Staff reviewed several recent variances for schools and community centres that are in
residential neighbourhoods and determined that a reduction of the distance to residential
properties is appropriate with several installed signs without complaints in the past few years.
The sign bylaw regulates digital signs to be turned off or sufficiently dimmed overnight.
Staff are proposing to reduce the distance of signs with automatic change in copy to
residentially zone lots to be 20 metres when oriented perpendicular to the street and 30 metres
otherwise instead of 100 metres. Staff are also proposing to reduce the radius for the sign
variance circulation notices to 60 metres. The circulation will remain at 120 metres for sign
bylaw amendments which are more significant applications. The current sign variance process
has been in effect since 2020.
At that time, sign variances were delegated to staff with some exceptions,
including a staff recommendation of refusal or a community concern that could not be resolved.
Based on the variance request process, community comments typically come from those in close proximity to the sign.
Staff also received community feedback from a notice recipient beyond 60 metres
that the notification distance is excessive and wasteful of city resources.
staff recommend a 60 meter circulation distance for variances to continue to
provide notice to properties affected staff are proposing to remove the annual
renewal for home develop new home development signs as staff have
determined that there is no added value to an annual renewal this will
streamline the process for both staff and home builders permits for new home
development signs will remain valid for a period of four years.
There were three engagement opportunities in January of 2024, a virtual meeting with
the Waterloo Region Association of Realtors, a discussion at the Kitchener Development
Liaison Committee meeting, and a virtual community meeting, including members from the sign industry.
Overall feedback was positive, and staff adjusted the proposed bylaw to address concerns about
the effective date and to clarify the size of lettering for the date or day of the week
for the special event directional signs.
The proposed amendments to the sign bylaw align with the purpose of the sign bylaw by
ensuring signs are appropriate in size, number and location to the type of activity to which
they pertain.
These amendments also aim to reduce excessive boulevard signage, thereby reducing visual
clutter and distractions for pedestrians and motorists. The proposed amendments are
minor and technical and staff are recommending approval of the proposed
sign bylaw amendment. The bylaw is proposed to come into effect on July 1st,
2024 to allow realtors and other special event providers sufficient time to
produce new signs.
